title: Pineapples Weren't Bought to Be Eaten
hook: In 18th-century England, a pineapple was something you showed off at parties
summary: One estimate puts the cost of growing a single pineapple in 18th-century England at about the price of a new coach. They were for showing off at parties more than for eating.

text: One historian estimates that growing a single pineapple cost about as much as a new carriage.

panels.text: One fruit for the price of a carriage? I'd rather just buy one.

text: The finest pineapples spent weeks going around evening parties in the city.

panels.text: Pineapples mean hospitality, right? Apparently not.

text: The story that colonial American captains put a pineapple at the door to welcome guests doesn't appear in records from the time.
